Criminal Case No. 14483 of 2023 Keshavdutt Sharma Versus The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others Appearance: Mr. Sarvesh Kumar Sharma - Advocate for the petitione Mr. Saket Udeniya - Govt. Advocate for respondent/Sta Order
texts.facts: The present petition has been preferred by the petitioners under Section 528 of the BNSS, 2023, seeking quashment of FIR registered at Crime No.121/2023 at Police Station - Ambah, District -Morena for the offence under Sections 420, 272 and 273 of IPC. 2. The allegations against the applicant/accused, in short, are that on 17/02/2023, Food Safety Officer Kiran Senger, along with other officials, conducted an inspection at Tyagi Cold, Pinhat Road, Ambah, Tehsil and District Morena, for the purpose of inspecting food items and collecting samples. During the inspection, mawa was found being made in ten cauldrons. Approximately 50 liters of separated milk was kept in a pan, and about 15 kg of refined palm oil was kept in an aluminum can. The employees were observed making mawa by mixing refined palm oil into the separated milk. The seller claimed that he makes and sells mawa by mixing separated NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:31002 2 MCRC-14483-2023 milk and refined palm kernel oil at the request of the customer. However, no customer was present at the spot to give such a statement, nor was any demand letter presented by the seller on the spot to prove that the seller manufactures mawa by mixing oil on the customer's request. 500 kg of mawa was kept ready there, which, according to the seller, was of the same quality. Samples of the milk, mawa, and refined palm kernel oil kept there were taken under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The remaining mawa and the adulterated refined palm kernel oil were duly seized and given in the safe custody of the seller, Keshav Dutt Sharma. By manufacturing and selling mawa by mixing refined palm kernel oil, it appears that the accused is, apart from gaining unethical economic benefits from this business, also compromising public health and cheating the public, whereas, the Government has issued instructions for strict action against adulterators. Hence, an F.I.R. was requested to be registered Keshavdutt Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 28 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147468185/ 1 against the concerned Keshav Dutt Sharma. Based on the above application, a prima facie offence under Sections 420, 272, and 273 of the Indian Penal Code was registered and taken up for investigation.

Counsel for the petitioner submits that earlier petitioner was granted anticipatory bail considering the following grounds:- "For the offence of cheating under Section 420 IPC, ingredients of Section 415 of IPC have to be fulfilled. There must be a representation which is false which representation must lead a person to act in a manner which causes him loss or to act in a manner in which he would not have otherwise acted but for the false representation. NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:31002 3 MCRC-14483-2023 Learned counsel for the applicant submits that where there is a special law to deal with the specific situation the resort can not be taken into the general law as the same is violative of the maxim 'generalia specilibus non derogant' or the general law shall not apply in derogation to the special law. 9. The parameters for quashing criminal proceedings have been crystallized in the case of State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal , 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335, where the Hon'ble Supreme Court enumerated seven categories of cases warranting interference. Unless the allegations in the F.I.R., even if taken at face value, do not constitute any offence or are absurd, mala fide , or inherently improbable, the Court should refrain from quashing.
